world.label: World / environment
world.description: Historical systems, institutions, places, traditions, languages, religions, media environments, technologies, and other conditions in which people live and create.

person.label: Person / formation
person.description: Creators as human beings: reading, education, profession, mentors, social circles, travel, lived events, beliefs, and documented formative experience.

work.label: Work / expression
work.description: Specific books, stories, poems, films, games, and other works in which inherited material is transformed, quoted, rejected, adapted, or recombined.

textual_transmission.label: Textual / explicit transmission
textual_transmission.description: A creator or work encounters, cites, adapts, alludes to, quotes, reuses, or otherwise demonstrably receives material from an earlier source.

lived_experience.label: Lived experience
lived_experience.description: Documented events or circumstances directly experienced by a creator, without assuming psychological causation.

historical_social_context.label: Historical / social context
historical_social_context.description: A broader historical, economic, political, institutional, geographic, or social condition relevant to the creator or work.

intellectual_social_formation.label: Intellectual / social formation
intellectual_social_formation.description: Education, profession, mentors, creative circles, religion, philosophy, editorial environments, and other institutions or relationships that shape practice.

formal_genre_inheritance.label: Formal / genre inheritance
formal_genre_inheritance.description: Transmission of genre conventions, narrative structures, style, artistic form, or established compositional practice.

authorship_publication.label: Authorship / publication lineage
authorship_publication.description: Authorship, serialization, collection, series order, publication history, and same-author continuity. These are lineage facts, not influence claims.

reaction_against.label: Reaction against
reaction_against.description: A creator or work is explicitly shaped by resisting, reversing, parodying, rebutting, or departing from an earlier source or convention.

context_hierarchy.label: Context hierarchy
context_hierarchy.description: A broad process, system, or recurring pattern contains a more specific historical case. This expresses abstraction, not causal influence.

comparison.label: Comparison only
comparison.description: A useful resemblance with no claim that transmission occurred.

other.label: Other / unclassified
other.description: Relationship not yet mapped into the controlled mechanism vocabulary.

context_scopes.system: Large historical, institutional, economic, political, or cultural system.
context_scopes.pattern: Recurring social, geographic, artistic, or historical pattern that can appear in multiple cases.
context_scopes.tradition: Ongoing cultural, linguistic, religious, oral, artistic, or intellectual tradition.
context_scopes.event: Specific historically significant event that deserves independent representation.
context_scopes.case: Specific local or biographical manifestation of a broader system or pattern.
context_scopes.episode: Person-specific episode. Normally keep this in person/work evidence and the side dossier rather than as a World node; retain a standalone node only when the event has independent historical or cultural significance.
context_scopes.unscoped: Not yet assigned an abstraction level.

evidence_classes.explicit: Creator or tradition-bearer directly identifies the source, intention, reaction, or formative relationship.
evidence_classes.direct_textual: Quotation, adaptation, title source, named allusion, demonstrable reuse, or similarly close textual relation.
evidence_classes.biographical: Letters, diaries, education, profession, travel, relationships, military service, or other documented life circumstances.
evidence_classes.historical_context: Documented circumstance relevant to formation, setting, or subject matter without automatic psychological causation.
evidence_classes.inferred: Chronology, access, and specificity make a hypothesis plausible but not established.

editorial_rules: Chronology is necessary but not sufficient evidence.
Separate work-level formation from person-level formation.
Prefer reusable context nodes over one-person biography bubbles.
World/context nodes should name the shared external phenomenon itself; do not append one creator's participation to the node label.
Person-specific travel, jobs, anecdotes, and other episodes normally belong in relationship evidence and the person dossier, not as history/context nodes.
Keep specific events when they are independently significant or directly enter a work.
Model translations, collectors, teachers, editors, archives, adaptations, and other mediators when they materially shape transmission.
Do not convert lived experience into psychological causation without evidence.
Graph density is not cultural importance.
Sparse documentation may reflect language, digitization, archival survival, collection history, or access bias.
A model-generated connection begins as candidate or inference and cannot verify itself.
